pairs.subject: media-playback
pairs.evidence: packages/voice-tts/src/react/utterance.ts:153 Pipelined utterance playback chains chunk execution sequentially off predecessor resolution rather than scheduling media intervals against an authoritative playback clock.

techniques.evidence: packages/voice-tts/src/react/utterance.ts:153 Pipelined audio chunk playback is chained sequentially off predecessor completion rather than scheduled against an authoritative timeline clock.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/useTts.ts:23 The transport state vocabulary lacks buffering, stalled, ready, and ended states, and awaited playback transitions carry no watchdogs.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/utterance.ts:175 Minted chunk object URLs are accumulated across the utterance and only released on completion or stop, violating reap-on-replace.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/useTts.ts:224 Playback progress is tracked solely as reactive React state without an authoritative clock reference outside the reactive tree.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/useTts.ts:219 Lookahead buffer depth is hardcoded to a static default rather than derived from measured production time and jitter dispersion percentiles.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/utterance.ts:226 Steering input immediately aborts in-flight generation without an append option, shallow acknowledgement lane, or margin-derived discard budget.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/useTts.ts:323 Playback directly instantiates HTMLAudioElement without an engine adapter interface or declared playback capabilities.
packages/voice-tts/src/react/useTts.ts:333 Playback error terminates the utterance without a playback fallback ladder, audio source blacklist, or transition treatment.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard states that media-playback does not own the speech channel (which belongs to voice-io), yet generated-supply-margin explicitly highlights 'synthesized speech played as it is produced' as a primary motivating use case; the standard should define the architectural boundary between voice-io (synthesis/dialogue generation) and media-playback (pipelined chunk playback, transport state machine, and object-URL lifecycle in browser speech hooks).

pairs.subject: media-playback
pairs.evidence: app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:56 The transport button collapses pause into stop by immediately terminating playback and surrendering utterance position when pressed during speech.

techniques.evidence: app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:56 The transport control collapses stop and pause by surrendering position and aborting speech on stop rather than pausing.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:66 Voice mode tracks active speaking via binary turn ID comparison without an authoritative playback clock or playhead time.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:87 Interrupting an ongoing spoken turn immediately aborts playback rather than offering an append option or shallow acknowledgement lane.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:51 Spoken replies are triggered as discrete isolated utterances rather than scheduled against a continuous timeline.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:101 The transport button binds directly to the high-level CompanionSpeech interface without querying declared engine capabilities.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:73 The UI displays a simple waiting indicator when throttled rather than calculating or exposing supply margin metrics.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/VoicePlayback.tsx:86 Playback failures present localized error copy but lack a playback fallback ladder or source blacklist.
app/features/shell/companion/voice/CompanionVoiceMode.tsx:131 Playback invocation via keyboard shortcuts relies on unmount cleanup without managing element or stream resources directly.

pairs.registryProposal: The transport-contract standard requires distinguishing paused from buffering and stopped, but spoken turn UI surfaces intentionally collapse stop and pause into a single toggle because speech turns are ephemeral and non-seekable; the standard should specify whether turn-based speech surfaces are exempt from the pause-vs-stop requirement or how speech transport should model intent surrender.
